projects.title: SatuRT
projects.description: Neighborhood association information system built with Laravel, Alpine.js, and Tailwind CSS for resident services and administrative workflows.
projects.content:
## Overview

SatuRT was built as a campus project for neighborhood administration workflows. The project combined backend data handling, role-aware access, and responsive interface work in one structured web system.

## Role

Full-stack system design and implementation — from database schema to responsive UI.

## Architecture

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend | Alpine.js + Tailwind CSS | Interactive UI with utility styling |
| Backend | Laravel (PHP MVC) | Request handling, auth, business logic |
| Database | MySQL | Structured data storage |

## Key Features

- **Resident Data Management** — Organized resident records in a structured flow so operators could update, review, and maintain data with less friction
- **Family Administration Workflow** — Family-linked data management to reflect real administrative relationships inside the application
- **Document and Service Requests** — Workflow-oriented actions for day-to-day administrative tasks instead of limiting the system to static data storage
- **Responsive Interface** — Responsive screens that keep operational tasks usable across smaller and larger devices

## Challenges

- Balancing data structure, administrative flow, and interface simplicity required frequent iteration
- Keeping authorization predictable across routes and features was important as the system scope expanded

## Outcome

Delivered a structured community information system with data management, decision support, document requests, and responsive interface work.

projects.title: Cinema Microservice
projects.description: Cinema-domain backend built as a .NET microservice experiment with service separation, caching, messaging, and containerized local development.
projects.content:
## Overview

Cinema Microservice was a backend-focused project used to expand public work into .NET and service-oriented architecture. The goal was to explore how service boundaries, caching, and messaging fit into a modular backend system.

## Role

.NET backend implementation and service structure exploration.

## Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            API Gateway                  │
└──────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────┘
       │          │          │
  ┌────▼────┐ ┌───▼───┐ ┌───▼────┐
  │  Auth   │ │ Movie │ │Booking │
  │ Service │ │Service│ │Service │
  └────┬────┘ └───┬───┘ └───┬────┘
       │          │          │
  ┌────▼──────────▼──────────▼────┐
  │     Infrastructure Layer      │
  │  ┌─────┐  ┌───────┐  ┌─────┐ │
  │  │ MSSQL│  │ Redis │  │ NATS│ │
  │  └─────┘  └───────┘  └─────┘ │
  └───────────────────────────────┘
```

| Component | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | .NET + C# | Type-safe backend framework |
| ORM | Entity Framework Core | Database access layer |
| Database | MSSQL | Persistent data storage |
| Cache | Redis | Response caching, session data |
| Messaging | NATS | Inter-service communication |
| Container | Docker Compose | Local development environment |

## Key Features

- **Service-Oriented Backend Structure** — Split the domain into clearer service boundaries for better separation of concerns
- **Caching and Messaging Integration** — Added Redis and NATS to explore supporting infrastructure patterns
- **Containerized Development Workflow** — Used Docker to keep the stack easier to run and reproduce consistently

## Challenges

- Service-oriented architecture introduces more coordination overhead than a single application backend
- Learning and integrating unfamiliar infrastructure components required more deliberate debugging

## Outcome

Expanded public backend work beyond PHP and TypeScript by building service-oriented architecture with modern .NET tooling.

projects.title: Vacation REST API
projects.description: TypeScript REST API starter built with NestJS, Prisma, Docker, and a structured backend project layout.
projects.content:
## Overview

Vacation REST API was built as a backend starter project focused on maintainable API structure. The project reflects the kind of backend structure worth repeating — clear modules, predictable data access, and a local workflow that can be continued without large setup differences.

## Role

Backend architecture and API implementation.

## Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│           NestJS Application         │
│  ┌────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐  │
│  │ Controllers │  │   Services    │  │
│  └─────┬──────┘  └──────┬────────┘  │
│        │                │           │
│  ┌─────▼────────────────▼────────┐  │
│  │         Prisma ORM            │  │
│  └─────────────┬─────────────────┘  │
└────────────────┼────────────────────┘
                 │
  ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐
  │        PostgreSQL            │
  └─────────────────────────────┘
```

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | NestJS | Modular backend structure |
| ORM | Prisma | Schema-driven data access |
| Database | PostgreSQL | Persistent storage |
| Container | Docker | Reproducible dev environment |

## Key Features

- **Structured REST API Modules** — Organized the API into services and controllers with clear boundaries
- **Schema-Driven Data Access** — Used Prisma to keep schema and query handling explicit and maintainable
- **Docker-Based Environment Setup** — Reduced setup friction by making the local workflow easier to reproduce

## Challenges

- A starter still needs enough structure to be useful without becoming overengineered
- Aligning data modeling, service boundaries, and developer setup required intentional tradeoffs

## Outcome

Established a maintainable backend starter with modular services, database access, and deployment-ready tooling.

projects.title: Inventory JTI
projects.description: Inventory management system for item tracking, loan management, reporting, and database-backed operations in a PHP MVC structure.
projects.content:
## Overview

Inventory JTI focused on inventory operations such as item tracking, stock control, borrowing flow, and reporting. The system was designed around practical operational use rather than visual presentation alone.

## Role

System implementation and CRUD workflow development.

## Architecture

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend | HTML/CSS/JavaScript | Interface rendering |
| Backend | PHP MVC | Request handling, business logic |
| Database | MySQL | Structured data storage |

## Key Features

- **Item and Stock Management** — Built CRUD flows for managing inventory records with structured data handling
- **Loan Workflow Handling** — Added borrowing-related flow to reflect real movement of inventory items
- **Reporting-Oriented Data Structure** — Supported reporting and record review for operational tracking

## Challenges

- Inventory systems require careful handling of state changes across stock, borrowing, and reporting
- Keeping CRUD implementation simple while preserving operational usefulness took iteration

## Outcome

Delivered a structured web system that supports inventory records, loan flows, and reporting.

projects.title: Ngejoblist
projects.description: Job-platform backend project focused on authentication, job management, company workflows, and production-style API structure.
projects.content:
## Overview

Ngejoblist is a backend platform project built around job-management workflows, role-aware platform logic, and product-oriented API structure. The project pushed backend practice into a more product-oriented platform direction.

## Role

Backend implementation and platform workflow development.

## Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              API Gateway                │
└──────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────┘
       │          │          │
  ┌────▼────┐ ┌───▼───┐ ┌───▼────┐
  │  Auth   │ │ Jobs  │ │Companies│
  │ Module  │ │Module │ │ Module  │
  └────┬────┘ └───┬───┘ └───┬────┘
       │          │          │
  ┌────▼──────────▼──────────▼────┐
  │         Prisma ORM            │
  └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                  │
  ┌───────────────▼───────────────┐
  │          PostgreSQL            │
  └───────────────────────────────┘
```

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Auth | JWT + Role-based access control |
| Jobs | Job listings, applications, filtering |
| Companies | Company profiles, verification |

## Key Features

- **Authentication Workflow** — JWT-based auth with role-aware platform behavior
- **Role-Aware Platform Logic** — Structured the application so users and companies interact through clearer workflow rules
- **Job Management Flow** — Implemented domain logic around job-related operations beyond basic CRUD

## Challenges

- Platform-style features introduce more interconnected rules than a simpler internal tool backend
- Domain logic, authentication, and filtering needed to stay readable as the feature surface grew

## Outcome

Broadened public API work into a more product-oriented platform with structured modules and business-domain features.

projects.title: Cat Stories
projects.description: Cat adoption data management system built with React on the frontend and Express, Knex, Swagger, and SQL-backed workflows on the backend.
projects.content:
## Overview

Cat Stories Management System was a fuller web application that combined frontend structure, backend API work, validation, and database-backed management flow. It reinforced the value of treating validation and documentation as part of system quality.

## Role

Backend-focused implementation with database and API work.

## Architecture

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend | React | Interactive UI components |
| Backend | Express.js | API endpoints, middleware |
| ORM | Knex.js | Query builder, migrations |
| Docs | Swagger | API documentation |
| Database | MSSQL | Persistent data storage |

## Key Features

- **CRUD-Oriented Backend API** — Implemented CRUD flow for adoption-related records with explicit data handling
- **Validation and Data Integrity** — Added validation mechanisms so requests remained predictable
- **Swagger Documentation** — Documented the API surface to make the backend understandable for integration

## Challenges

- Keeping the backend flow explicit while supporting a larger feature surface required discipline
- Documenting and validating the API added extra work but improved clarity significantly

## Outcome

Built a more complete web application structure with frontend, backend, validation, and documented API flow.
